acceptance.text: What the plugin has today for the life of a change after review: Job kinds (internal/job), the feed (internal/orchestrator, grid worker next), how a Job ends after a reviewer verdict, whether anything merges onto a branch. Name what is missing for landing.

What the scripts do that the plugin would need, read from land.sh, landbatch.sh, landrun.sh, collect.sh, eject2fix.sh, skip2merge.sh: list the rules (holds, stacks, M- merge lanes, ejects, flake reruns, cross-repo check, generated-file conflicts, attribution check, NOT DONE closing) and say for each whether it belongs in a land Job, in the project's workflow note (brain), or disappears with per-change landing.

Design of a land Job: posted by the orchestrator when a change's review passes; depends on the change's Job and on the land Jobs of changes it stacks on; runs as a runner (no agent needed for the green path): merge onto the current target in a worktree, run the project's check command (from the brain, e.g. make check), fast-forward or merge on green. Parallel: speculative stacking (test N on main+pending N-1, like a merge queue) or test each on main and rebase-check at merge; pick one with numbers from this box (12 cores, full check time from the land logs). A red check: rerun the failing tests alone; flake -> lands and posts a flake Job; real -> the land Job fails and posts a fix Job for the builder. Conflict -> a merge Job for a builder.
Capacity: how a land Job gets CPU before builders on one machine with the worker's existing launch path (priority between Job kinds, a slot for check Jobs), without adding a cap on agents.

Moving this build onto Grid: what else the scripts do (multi-account lanes, limit switching, planners, maps, end reviews) and which plugin features already cover it; an order of steps to move, smallest first, and what has to land before the cutover (23 Nov).
Lane plan: plugin lanes with repo, model/effort, files, acceptance rows and dependencies; then the app pieces (Feed shows land Jobs).

out_of_scope: push, touch <gmf>, <root-home>, other users' homes, pkill -f; never edit the scripts in <hand> (read only)
A refused Bash call is not the end - rerun it as one plain command and go on
No attribution lines in commits or files
title: R-land-job-type: landing as a first-class Grid Job, so the build can run on Grid itself
